digest.headline: OpenAI teases a math-proving "Astra" days before the EU AI Act's transparency rules go live, while MCP's biggest-ever spec update lands inside Claude and DeepSeek quietly beats its own flagship with a Flash model
digest.summary: OpenAI revealed that an internal version of its next major model, Astra, resolved ten decades-old open problems in math and theoretical computer science — including the first-ever construction of a non-sofic group — publishing machine-checkable Lean proofs for about $2,000 in compute; Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers said he'd recommend one of the proofs for a top journal without hesitation. Two days later, the EU's AI Act transparency and GPAI obligations became enforceable, requiring chatbots to disclose they're AI and deepfakes to carry machine-readable marks. On the infrastructure side, Anthropic finished rolling MCP's stateless 2026-07-28 spec into Claude, adding a private-network "MCP tunnels" research preview, and DeepSeek's re-post-trained V4-Flash-0731 beat its own larger V4-Pro on all nine published benchmarks. Codex and Pi both shipped harness updates, and Claude Sonnet 5's intro pricing quietly starts a 50% step-up on September 1.

stories.title: OpenAI's unreleased Astra model solves 10 open math problems, publishes the proofs
stories.dek: An internal version of OpenAI's next major model, Astra, resolved ten problems in high-dimensional geometry, group theory, coding theory, and extremal combinatorics that had seen no progress in at least a decade — including the first explicit construction of a non-sofic group, a question open since Gromov coined the term in 1999. OpenAI published a 249-page manuscript with machine-checkable Lean 4 certificates on GitHub, putting the total compute cost at roughly $2,000.
stories.whyItMatters: OpenAI is debuting its next flagship through verifiable mathematical proof rather than benchmark scores — Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers said he'd recommend one of the results for a top journal without hesitation, and the $2,000 price tag suggests frontier-math research is becoming compute-scalable rather than talent-limited.

stories.title: EU AI Act transparency rules become enforceable, with fines up to €15M
stories.dek: As of August 2, the European Commission's AI Office and national authorities began enforcing the AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties: chatbots must disclose they're AI rather than human, and deepfakes must carry machine-readable marks. Providers face fines up to €15 million or 3% of global turnover; a shorter extension to December 2 applies to marking obligations for generative systems already on the market before August 2.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the day EU AI enforcement stops being theoretical — any product built on a chatbot or generative model serving EU users needs disclosure and provenance marking in place now, not on a roadmap.

stories.title: MCP's stateless spec finishes rolling into Claude, plus a private-network tunnels preview
stories.dek: Anthropic detailed how Claude is adopting the finalized MCP 2026-07-28 specification: a stateless request/response core suited to serverless and edge deployment, standardized Apps and Tasks extensions, and auth hardened to production OAuth 2.0/OIDC so enterprises can connect Entra or Okta directly. Claude's connectors directory now lists over 950 MCP servers, and MCP SDK downloads are up 4x this year to 400M+ monthly.
stories.whyItMatters: This is MCP's biggest revision since launch, and Claude shipping full support the same week as the spec finalizes signals the stateless, load-balancer-friendly transport is now the real target for anyone running a server at scale.

stories.title: DeepSeek's re-trained V4-Flash-0731 beats its own bigger V4-Pro on every published benchmark
stories.dek: DeepSeek moved V4-Flash out of preview into public beta as a re-post-trained 284B-total/13B-active checkpoint. Terminal-Bench 2.1 jumped from 61.8 to 82.7 and DeepSWE rose 7.5x over the preview build; Artificial Analysis independently measured the release at 50 on its Intelligence Index, 6 points ahead of the larger V4-Pro, while using about 12% fewer output tokens to complete the eval suite.
stories.whyItMatters: A 13B-active model outscoring its own 1.6T flagship on agentic coding work is a strong signal that post-training gains, not raw parameter count, are now the cheaper lever for frontier-adjacent performance — though all the agent-benchmark numbers are still vendor-run on DeepSeek's own harness, with no third-party reproduction yet.

stories.title: Claude Sonnet 5's intro pricing ends August 31 — a 50% step-up on September 1
stories.dek: Sonnet 5 has been running introductory API pricing of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens since its June 30 launch. That rate expires August 31; standard pricing of $3/$15 per Mtok takes effect September 1, a flat 50% increase for anyone still on the intro rate.
stories.whyItMatters: Any team that sized its Sonnet 5 budget off launch pricing should re-run the math before September 1 — this is a real cost change, not a benchmark footnote.

harness.notes: Still the latest stable release: 2.1.219 made Claude Opus 5 the default Opus model (1M context) and raised default subagent nesting depth from 1 to 3; 2.1.220 followed with bug fixes and reliability improvements. Separately, Claude's shared MCP layer finished adopting the 2026-07-28 spec, adding a private-network "MCP tunnels" research preview usable from Claude Code.

Adds named sessions (via /new or /clear) with pinning and side-conversation switching, Agent Plugins manifests plus workspace plugin publishing, paginated thread history with temporary forks, app-server connections to remote Code Mode hosts over WebSocket, standalone web search for compatible model providers, and discovery of executor-provided skills.

Adds credential export for external clients and fixes forced model-availability refreshes that stayed blocked behind a stalled earlier refresh. Follows 0.82.1's Claude Opus 5 support on Anthropic and Amazon Bedrock a few days earlier.

extensions.name: MCP tunnels
extensions.blurb: Lets Claude connect to MCP servers inside a private network with no inbound firewall rules, public endpoints, or IP allowlisting — teams can expose internal tools to Claude without putting them on the public internet.

extensions.name: Record a Skill
extensions.blurb: Demonstrate a task on screen while narrating the rules and exceptions, and Claude Desktop (Pro/Max/Team) converts the recording into a reusable Skill — no private model training on the recording involved.

extensions.name: DeepTutor v1.5.7
extensions.blurb: Adds a one-click store of 45 curated hosted MCP servers (Notion, Linear, Sentry via OAuth 2.1/PKCE, tokens resolved in memory rather than written to config) plus 101 sandboxed CLI tools sourced from the CLI-Anything registries.

tips.title: "Pencil and paper mode" stops your agent from coding before you're ready
tips.body: Prepending "Stay in pencil and paper mode" (or just "Pencil and paper mode") to a request gets Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity to discuss and plan before touching any files — it works even in cases where softer phrasing like "what would be involved" fails to stop premature edits. Example: "Stay in pencil and paper mode. What would be involved in removing the 'counter' readout in the top header?" The same trick works for any task where you want analysis before action, not just coding.

tips.title: Give autonomous tasks a way to verify themselves, not just a way to run
tips.body: For any task you want Claude Code to run unattended, close the write-test cycle explicitly — give it a command or check it can run itself to confirm the change worked, rather than a task that ends at "wrote the code." Without a verification step baked in, autonomous runs tend to stop at plausible-looking output instead of confirmed-working output.

tips.title: Write a handoff document before a session gets unwieldy, not after
tips.body: When a long session's context starts to degrade, have Claude write a handoff file first — what it tried, what worked, what didn't — so a fresh session can resume without re-deriving everything. The /handoff command automates this, capturing goals, progress, and next steps; treat it as a checkpoint to reach for proactively rather than a recovery step for after things go sideways.
